title: The Man Who Carried His Bullock on His Head (HI)
summary: Birbal meets a traveler carrying his luggage and riding an oxcart, claiming he is sparing the animals. Birbal exposes the comedy of misplaced self-sacrifice.
full_text:
While traveling along the dusty highway between Agra and Mathura, Emperor Akbar and Birbal rode past a bullock cart loaded with sacks of grain. Inside the cart sat a well-dressed passenger who was holding a heavy, wooden iron-banded trunk firmly balanced upon his own head!

The two bullocks were straining to pull the heavy cart through the deep dust.

Akbar reined in his horse in complete disbelief: 'Look at that man, Birbal! He is sitting inside the cart, yet he is carrying his heavy iron trunk upon his own head! Is he mad?'

Akbar rode alongside the cart and called out: 'Friend! Why on earth are you carrying that heavy iron trunk on your head instead of placing it on the floor of the cart?'

The passenger wiped sweat from his eyes and replied with sincere piety:

'Noble rider! My heart is full of tender compassion! These two poor bullocks are already pulling this heavy cart and thirty sacks of grain!

'If I placed this heavy iron trunk on the floor of the cart as well, it would increase the weight and break the poor animals' backs!

'So I carry the trunk upon my own head, so that I bear its weight myself and spare the poor beasts!'

Akbar stared in astonishment, then burst into a roar of laughter.

Birbal smiled and explained to the passenger:

'Brother, think for one second! Whether you place the trunk on the wooden floor of the cart, or hold it upon your own head—are you not sitting inside the cart?

'Your body is supported by the cart, and the cart is pulled entirely by the bullocks! Every ounce of weight on your head presses down through your body onto the cart, and onto the bullocks' shoulders!

'You are not sparing the bullocks a single grain of weight; you are merely giving yourself a terrible headache and looking like a premier fool!'

The passenger looked down at the cart floor, then up at his trunk, and sheepishly placed the trunk down with a sigh of relief.

Akbar laughed all the way back to Agra, remarking that many men endure useless misery in life because they do not understand the simple laws of reality.
